showreel-11-springs.caption:
Why do some buttons feel expensive? 🫧

Same button, same duration. One eases and stops dead; the other springs: it overshoots a touch and settles, like a real object. CSS does this natively with linear(), in Chrome, Firefox and Safari since 2023.
Save it for your next interface, or send it to whoever builds your buttons.

showreel-12-inp.caption:
Your site loads fast. So why does it feel slow? ⚡

It's probably INP, Interaction to Next Paint: the time from a tap to the next frame on screen. Google rates over 500 ms as poor and 200 ms or less as good. The usual cause is one long JavaScript task blocking the main thread. Split it up so the browser can paint in between.
Save it for your next speed check, or send it to whoever owns your site's performance.

showreel-13-popup.caption:
Why does your popup just snap in? ✨

CSS can't transition from display: none, so a popup appears on a single frame. @starting-style gives it a first state (opacity 0, scale .9) to animate from, so it glides in. Works in Chrome, Firefox and Safari (Baseline 2024). One block, no JavaScript.
Save it for your next modal, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-14-stagger.caption:
Why does your list feel so flat? 🧱

When every row runs the same entrance at the same moment, the list lands as one block. Keep the animation and delay each row by its index: animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms), with --i set to 0, 1, 2… on each row. Now the eye reads it top to bottom. Works on lists, grids and menus. Pure CSS, no library.
Save it for your next list, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-15-transform.caption:
Why does your animation stutter? 🐢

Animating left (or width, top, margin) makes the browser redo layout and paint on every frame. Miss the ~16.7 ms frame budget and frames drop. Move it with transform instead: it's handled in compositing, so layout and paint are skipped. Same move, smooth. (Opacity works the same way.)
Save it for your next animation, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-16-balance.caption:
Why does your headline break so badly? ✍️

When a heading wraps, the browser fills each line as far as it can, so one word often ends up alone on the last line. Add text-wrap: balance and the browser evens out the line lengths instead. One line of CSS on your h1, h2 and h3; works in every major browser, for headings up to six lines in Chromium (ten in Firefox).
Save it for your next landing page, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-17-smooth.caption:
Why does your page jump when you tap a link? 🪂

An in-page link (#pricing, #faq) teleports the page by default, so people lose their place. Add scroll-behavior: smooth to html and the page glides to the section instead. Put it inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so anyone who turns motion off keeps the instant jump. One line of CSS, works in every major browser.
Save it for your next landing page, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-18-overscroll.caption:
Why does the page scroll, behind your popup? 📜

Scroll to the end of a list inside a modal, menu or bottom sheet and the scroll passes on to the page underneath. That's scroll chaining. Add overscroll-behavior: contain to the popup's scrolling element and the scroll stops at its edge; the page stays put. One line of CSS, in every major browser. (It only applies to an element that actually scrolls.)
Save it for your next modal, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-19-numbers.caption:
Why do your numbers wiggle when they change? ⏱️

Most fonts give each digit its own width: a 1 is narrow, a 0 is wide. So a live timer, price or score shifts sideways every time a digit changes. Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and every digit takes the same width, so the number holds still. One line of CSS, in every major browser. (It uses the font's tabular figures, so the font needs them; most UI fonts have them.)
Save it for your next dashboard, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-20-hover.caption:
Why does your button stay lit after tapping? 👆

On a phone there's no mouse, so a tap counts as a hover. In some mobile browsers the :hover style then sticks after your finger lifts, until you tap somewhere else. Wrap your hover styles in @media (hover: hover) and only devices that can really hover (a mouse, a trackpad) get them; on a phone, a tap is just a tap. One media query, in every major browser. (A few Android phones report hover wrongly; add and (pointer: fine) to be safe. Keep an :active style for tap feedback.)
Save it for your next button, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

showreel-21-dvh.caption:
Why is your button cut off on phones? 📱

A full-screen hero set to height: 100vh is sized for the large viewport: the screen with the browser's address and tool bars hidden. When the bars are showing (as they are when a page first loads), the bottom of the hero sits under them, and so does your button. Use 100dvh instead: the dynamic viewport height follows the bars, so the hero fits the screen you can actually see. In every major browser since 2022. (dvh resizes as the bars move while scrolling; if that jump bothers you, 100svh is the stable, always-visible size.)
Save it for your next landing page, or send it to whoever builds your site.

showreel-22-squash.caption: Why do your photos look squashed? 📸 An is object-fit: fill by default: it fills its box exactly, so when the box has a different shape from the photo (a wide banner, a tall card on a phone), the picture is stretched to match. Add object-fit: cover and the image keeps its own shape: it still fills the whole box, and the edges that don't fit are cropped instead. Pick which part stays in view with object-position (center by default). Works in every major browser. Save it for your next card grid, or send it to whoever builds your site.

showreel-23-sideways.caption:
Why does your page slide sideways on phones? 📱

By default text only wraps at normal break points, like a space (overflow-wrap: normal). A long link, an email address or a code has none, so it sticks out past the screen and the whole page can be dragged sideways. Add overflow-wrap: anywhere and the browser may break that one long string at any point, but only when it would overflow; normal words still wrap at spaces. Unlike break-word, anywhere also lets a flex or grid item shrink to fit. Chrome 80+, Firefox 65+, Safari 15.4+.
Save it for your next blog or order page, or send it to whoever builds your site.

showreel-24-sticky.caption:
Why did your sticky header stop sticking? 📌

A sticky element sticks to its nearest ancestor with a scrolling mechanism, and overflow: hidden creates one even if that box never scrolls (MDN). So one wrapper with overflow: hidden captures your header, and it scrolls away with the page. Swap it for overflow: clip: the content is still clipped, but the box is not a scroll container, so the header sticks to the page again. Chrome 90+, Firefox 81+, Safari 16+. (No top value set? Sticky never sticks; check that first.)
Save it for the next time a header won't stick, or send it to whoever builds your site.

showreel-25-anchor.caption:
Why is your heading hiding under the header? 🔗

A link to #billing scrolls that heading to the very top of the page, right where your fixed header sits, so the header covers it. Add scroll-padding-top to the html element, about the height of your header: it tells the browser the top strip is covered, so every link jump (and scrollIntoView) stops below it. One rule fixes every link on the page. Chrome 69+, Firefox 68+, Safari 14.1+. (For a single target, scroll-margin-top on that heading does the same.)
Save it for your next docs or FAQ page, or send it to whoever builds your site.
keywords: anchor link hidden under fixed header

showreel-26-longname.caption:
Why does one long name break your card? 💳

Your name has overflow: hidden, white-space: nowrap and text-overflow: ellipsis, yet it still pushes the button out of the card. The name sits in a flex item, and a flex item's min-width is auto: its smallest allowed width is its content, here the whole one-line name. Add min-width: 0 to that flex item (the wrapper, not the text): it can shrink, and the ellipsis finally shows. Works in every browser (Chrome 21+, Firefox 34+, Safari 7+ have the auto minimum). overflow: hidden on the flex item does the same.
Save it for your next list or contact card, or send it to whoever builds your app.

showreel-27-keyboard.caption:
Why does your form show the wrong keyboard? 📱

A plain text field gets the phone's standard letter keyboard (inputmode="text" is the default), so for a one-time code, a PIN or an amount your user has to switch layouts and hunt for the digits. Add inputmode="numeric" and the phone opens a number pad: digits 0-9, one tap each. It only changes the keyboard, not what counts as valid, so keep your own checks. For emails and phone numbers use type="email" and type="tel". Chrome 66+, Firefox 95+, Safari 12.1+ (iOS 12.2+).
Save it for your next sign-up or checkout form, or send it to whoever builds yours.

showreel-28-thumb.caption:
Why does your thumb hit the wrong link? 👍

Menu links set in small text are often only about 16 px tall, so one fingertip covers two of them: you aim for Archive and get Delete. Give each link a real target: display: block and min-height: 44px. The text keeps its size; only the area you can tap grows. WCAG asks for targets of at least 24 × 24 CSS px (2.5.8, AA) and 44 × 44 for the best level (2.5.5, AAA). Works in every browser.
Save it for your next menu or footer, or send it to whoever builds your app.

showreel-29-flash.caption:
Why does your dark page flash white? 🌙

You browse in dark mode, tap a link, and the screen flashes white. Until a page's styles load, the browser shows a blank page in its default colors, and the default is light. Put <meta name="color-scheme" content="dark light"> in the <head>, before your CSS: the browser knows the page is dark from the first frame, so the blank is dark too, and default form boxes, checkboxes and scrollbars follow your theme. Supported in Chrome 81+, Firefox 96+ and Safari 12.1+.
Save it for your next dark theme, or send it to whoever builds your site.

showreel-33-carousel.caption:
Why does your carousel stop between photos? 📸

A row of photos with overflow-x: auto scrolls freely, so it stops wherever your finger lets go: half of one photo, half of the next. Add scroll-snap-type: x mandatory to the row and scroll-snap-align: center to each photo, and every swipe settles on one whole photo. No JavaScript, no library. Works in Chrome 69+, Safari 11+ and Firefox 99+.
Save it for your next product gallery, or send it to whoever built your carousel.

showreel-34-press.caption:
Why does your button feel dead on tap? 👆

With no :active style, a tap gives no sign it landed, so people tap again (and pay twice). While the button is pressed, shrink it to 96%, drop its shadow and darken it a touch, with a 0.12 s transition: it sinks under the finger and springs back. On iPhone, Safari only shows :active when the page listens for touches, so add ontouchstart to your <body>. scale works in Chrome 104+, Safari 14.1+ and Firefox 72+ (or use transform: scale(.96) for older browsers).
Save it for your next button, or send it to whoever built your checkout.
showreel-34-press.concept: transition: .12s + :active { scale: .96; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px #0006; filter: brightness(.92) } (a big Pay button that sinks under the finger); iPhone needs a touchstart listener

showreel-35-list.caption:
Why does your list jump when you delete a row? 🗑️

Remove a row from the page and every row under it snaps up in one frame, so the eye loses its place (and the next tap can land on the wrong message). Collapse it first: make the row a one-track grid (grid-template-rows: 1fr) with a 0.3 s transition, add a class that sets grid-template-rows: 0fr and opacity: 0, give its child overflow: hidden so it can shrink to nothing, and remove the row on transitionend. The rows below glide up instead of jumping. Animating grid tracks works in Chrome 107+, Safari 16+ and Firefox 66+.
Save it for your next list, or send it to whoever built your inbox.
showreel-35-list.concept: grid-template-rows 1fr -> 0fr + opacity 0 with a .3s transition, overflow: hidden on the child, then remove on transitionend (a deleted row collapses, the rows glide up instead of jumping)
showreel-35-list.about: E23 try 1 (dynamic fix, side by side) on E18 try 2 (dark): an inbox where every delete makes the rows below SNAP up (a red ghost, "jump!", DELETED counter), then BEFORE vs AFTER side by side deleting the same message at the same moment (snap vs collapse), one collapse replayed at 0.25x with its live curve and the height counting 68 → 0 px, and a rhythm of smooth deletes to the end.
